items.q: In unilateral conductive loss, Weber test lateralises where?
items.exp: Bone conducted sound seems louder in the conductively deaf ear because ambient masking is reduced and bone energy escapes less, so Weber points to the worse ear in conductive loss and to better ear in sensorineural loss.
r: Incorrect. Better ear lateralisation means sensorineural loss opposite.
Correct. Weber goes to the conductively deaf ear.
Incorrect. Midline suggests symmetry or normal.
Incorrect. Away would be sensorineural pattern.
items.kp: Conductive: Weber visits the bad ear.

items.q: Carhart notch in otosclerosis is best described as what?
items.exp: Stapes fixation artefactually depresses bone conduction at 2000 Hz, producing Carhart notch that disappears after successful surgery, proving it mechanical not cochlear. Noise notch instead hits air conduction at 4 kHz.
r: Incorrect. Four kilohertz air notch means noise trauma.
Correct. Bone dip at 2 kHz is Carhart notch.
Incorrect. Tympanometry stiffness is separate measure.
Incorrect. Drum is normal in otosclerosis.
items.kp: Two kilohertz bone dip equals Carhart.

items.q: Young woman with progressive bilateral conductive loss, normal drums and affected mother most likely has what?
items.exp: Autosomal dominant otosclerosis fixes stapes in young adults (female predominance, pregnancy worsening) with pristine drums. Glue ear shows effusion, cholesteatoma discharge, presbycusis sensorineural old age loss.
r: Incorrect. Effusion would dull the drum.
Correct. Familial stapes fixation is otosclerosis.
Incorrect. Cholesteatoma discharges and perforates.
Incorrect. Presbycusis is sensorineural ageing loss.
items.kp: Normal drum, young adult, family deafness: otosclerosis.

items.q: Definitive surgical correction for otosclerosis is what?
items.exp: Small fenestra stapedotomy bypasses fixed footplate with a piston between incus and oval window, closing air bone gap in most cases. Drum and mastoid operations address different diseases.
r: Incorrect. Myringoplasty closes perforations.
Correct. Piston prosthesis bypasses fixed stapes.
Incorrect. Mastoidectomy clears infected mastoid.
Incorrect. Grommets ventilate glue ear.
items.kp: Fixed stapes gets a piston bypass.

items.q: Schwartze sign in otitis media examination means what?
o: Pink blush behind drum from active otosclerotic bone
items.exp: Vascular spongy bone shining through the drum gives a flamingo pink Schwartze sign in active otosclerosis, present only in minority. Blue drum suggests haemotympanum or cholesterol granuloma.
r: Incorrect. Blue drum is blood or granuloma.
Correct. Pink blush means active otosclerotic foci.
Incorrect. White pearl is cholesteatoma.
Incorrect. Black debris is fungal canal disease.
items.kp: Pink glow behind drum: active otosclerosis.

items.q: Rinne test in conductive loss of the tested ear shows what?
items.exp: When conduction fails, bone conduction bypassing the block exceeds air conduction in that ear: Rinne negative, the classic conductive pattern. Normal and sensorineural ears keep air louder (positive).
r: Incorrect. Positive Rinne is normal or sensorineural.
Correct. Negative Rinne (bone over air) means conductive.
Incorrect. Equality is equivocal borderline.
Incorrect. Profound sensorineural loss gives false negative needing masking care.
items.kp: Bone beats air equals conductive loss.

items.q: Otosclerosis typically worsens during which physiological state?
items.exp: Hormonal changes of pregnancy classically accelerate otosclerosis progression, one reason women present more. Onset is young adult, not childhood, and progression is slow over years.
r: Incorrect. Male puberty is not the accelerator.
Correct. Pregnancy worsens otosclerosis.
Incorrect. Menopause is not the classic trigger.
Incorrect. Childhood fixation suggests congenital causes.

items.q: Tympanometry in stapes fixation typically shows which curve?
items.exp: Fixed ossicular chain stiffens the system giving shallow As tympanogram with preserved peak position but reduced compliance. Flat B is effusion; deep Ad is discontinuity or flaccid drum.
r: Incorrect. Flat B means fluid or perforation patterns.
Correct. Shallow stiff As curve in fixation.
Incorrect. Deep Ad means hypermobile system.
Incorrect. Curve is measurably shallow, not normal.

items.q: Traumatic ossicular discontinuity most commonly dislocates which ossicle joint?
items.exp: The incus, precariously suspended, dislocates at incudostapedial joint (or its body) after head trauma, causing immediate conductive gap with hypermobile tympanogram. Reconstruction uses ossiculoplasty prostheses.
r: Incorrect. Footplate fracture is rarer and risks inner ear.
Correct. Incudostapedial dislocation is commonest.
Incorrect. Malleus fixation is congenital or tympanosclerotic.
Incorrect. Round window injury causes sensorineural patterns.
items.kp: Trauma knocks the loosely hung incus loose.

items.q: Cochlear otosclerosis differs by adding which loss component?
items.exp: Foci invading cochlear capsule injure inner ear adding sensorineural (mixed) loss, limiting surgical gain and pushing toward amplification or implantation in severe disease.
r: Incorrect. Pure conductive is fenestral disease only.
Correct. Cochlear invasion adds sensorineural loss.
Incorrect. Lesion is capsular, not brain pathways.
Incorrect. Functional loss shows inconsistent audiometry.
items.kp: When otosclerosis invades cochlea, loss turns mixed.
